verdict.rationale: Reflect's AI palette (cmd+j on highlighted text) accepts free-form natural-language instructions and custom prompts, and filtered search lets users "chat" with notes to ask questions. However, the documented natural-language scope is limited to transforming selected text and querying notes; nothing shows natural language driving app operations such as creating, organizing, publishing, or navigating notes. Missing for 10: natural-language control of app actions beyond text transformation and Q&A, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: To use it, first highlight some text, and then press cmd j (or control j on Windows). That'll popup the AI palette.
You can also ask the AI palette anything you'd like using the open text field, and save it as a custom prompt to quickly call on again later.
After applying any desired filters to the search, you can also “chat” with those specific notes to ask questions and extract information.
